title: Random Silicon Sampling: Simulating Human Sub-Population Opinion Using a Large Language Model Based on Group-Level Demographic Information

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing LLM-generated voting choices and policy preferences for synthetic respondents conditioned on political party affiliation and ideology against actual American National Election Studies (ANES) survey data.

Evaluating the alignment of LLM-generated survey responses with actual ANES data across different racial and ethnic subgroups, and measuring divergences such as an exaggerated harmlessness tendency in specific racial groups.
Generating survey responses using synthetic personas conditioned on gender and comparing the resulting response distributions to real human poll data on various sensitive topics.
Assessing the model's ability to accurately replicate public opinion across different age brackets by prompting the LLM with age demographics and evaluating outputs against actual survey answers.
Prompting the LLM with church attendance demographics to simulate religious sub-populations and evaluating the accuracy of generated policy opinions against real respondent data.

Analyzing the LLM's systematic tendency to over-select innocuous or non-offensive answers on politically sensitive survey topics (e.g., gay marriage, refugee policies, racial diversity) compared to the actual empirical distribution of human opinions.
